modules.title: Lesson 1.1: Self & Identity (Je m'appelle / Je suis)
modules.canDo: Greet someone and introduce yourself using Je m'appelle or Je suis.
modules.concept: In French, 'Je m'appelle' literally means 'I call myself' and is the most natural way to share your name. 'Je suis' means 'I am'.

model.context: Meeting someone at a café in Lyon:
model.en: Hello! What is your name? — Hello! My name is Claire.

modules.title: Lesson 1.2: Professions & Identifying Things (Je suis / C'est)
modules.canDo: State professions without an article after être, and identify nouns with C'est un / une.
modules.concept: In French, drop 'un/une' when stating a profession directly after 'être': 'Je suis étudiant' (I am a student). Use 'C'est un' (masculine) or 'C'est une' (feminine) to point out things.

model.en: I am a student. She is a teacher.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Oui, je suis étudiant. Elle est professeur.
turns.en: Yes, I am a student. She is a teacher.

check.question: Which sentence naturally says 'I am a teacher' in French?

drills.explanation: Professions follow 'être' directly without an article.

modules.title: Lesson 1.3: Origins & Cities (venir de)
modules.canDo: Ask and say which city or country someone comes from using venir de.
modules.concept: Use 'venir de' (to come from) before cities: 'Je viens de Paris', 'Il vient de Lyon'. Before a vowel, 'de' becomes 'd'' ('d'Auckland').

model.en: Where are you from? — I come from Paris.

check.question: Which preposition links 'viens' to a city name like Paris?

drills.instruction: Match the sentence to its pattern
drills.explanation: 'venir de + place' states where someone comes from.

modules.title: Lesson 2.1: Everyday Present Actions (-er Verbs)
modules.canDo: Describe what you do or are doing right now using high-frequency -er verbs.
modules.concept: French uses one present tense for both 'I work' and 'I am working'. Regular '-er' verbs take: je -e, tu -es, il/elle -e, nous -ons.

model.en: What are you doing today? — I am studying French and working.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Je travaille et j'étudie le français.
turns.en: I am working and studying French.

options.text: 'Je' contracts to 'J'' before a vowel sound
Because 'étudie' is in the past tense

drills.explanation: Present actions follow subject + conjugated verb + detail.

modules.title: Lesson 2.2: Wellbeing & Feelings (Ça va / Je suis)
modules.canDo: Ask how someone is doing with Ça va and express feelings like happy, tired, or hungry.
modules.concept: Ask 'Ça va ?' and answer 'Ça va bien, merci !'. Use 'Je suis' + adjective ('content', 'fatigué'), but note French uses 'avoir' (to have) for hunger and thirst: 'J'ai faim' (I am hungry).

model.en: How are you? — I am doing well, thanks! I am happy.

turns.en: I am doing well, thanks! I am happy.

modules.title: Lesson 2.3: Past Actions (Passé Composé with avoir)
modules.canDo: Describe completed past actions using J'ai + -é past participles.
modules.concept: In spoken French, form the past with 'avoir' ('J'ai') plus the past participle. For '-er' verbs, simply replace '-er' with '-é': 'travailler' → 'J'ai travaillé'.

model.en: Did you work yesterday? — No, I studied French yesterday.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Non, j'ai étudié le français hier.

modules.title: Lesson 3.1: Current Location (au / à la / ici)
modules.canDo: Ask and state where people are located right now using au, à la, and à l'.
modules.concept: 'à' means 'at / in'. Before masculine 'le', 'à + le' always contracts to 'au' ('au bureau'). Before feminine 'la', it stays 'à la' ('à la maison').

model.context: Texting a colleague before a call:
model.en: Where are you? — I am at the office.

check.question: Why do we say 'au bureau' instead of 'à le bureau'?

options.text: 'à + le' always contracts to 'au' in French

modules.title: Lesson 3.2: Relative Position (dans / sur / sous)
modules.canDo: Describe whether an object is inside, on top of, under, or in front of a landmark.
modules.concept: French spatial prepositions link directly to the landmark noun: 'sur la table' (on the table), 'dans le sac' (in the bag), 'sous la chaise' (under the chair).

model.en: Where is the book? — The book is on the table.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Le livre est sur la table.
turns.en: The book is on the table.

modules.title: Lesson 3.3: Movement & Destinations (aller à / chez)
modules.canDo: Say where you are going using aller + au / à la / chez.
modules.concept: 'Je vais' (I go / I am going) uses 'au / à la / à' for places ('Je vais au bureau', 'Je vais à Paris') and 'chez' for a person's home ('chez moi' = to my place).
modules.pattern: [Subject] + vais / allons + au / à la / chez + [Destination]

model.en: Where are you going now? — I am going home. Tomorrow I am going to Paris.
model.literal: [I = Je] + [go = vais] + [to my place = chez moi]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Je vais chez moi. Demain je vais à Paris.
turns.en: I am going home. Tomorrow I am going to Paris.

modules.title: Lesson 4.1: Completed States (déjà fini / prêt)
modules.canDo: Announce that work or meals are already finished or ready using déjà + fini / prêt.
modules.concept: Pair 'est' with 'déjà' (already) and 'fini' (finished) or 'prêt' / 'prête' (ready) to announce completed milestones.

model.en: Is the work finished? — Yes, the work is already finished!
model.literal: [The work = Le travail] + [is = est] + [already = déjà] + [finished = fini]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Oui, le travail est déjà fini !
turns.en: Yes, the work is already finished!

prompts.situation: Announce that the work is already finished:

drills.instruction: Match the sentence to its pattern
drills.explanation: Completed states combine 'est + déjà + fini / prêt'.

modules.title: Lesson 4.2: Suggestions & Obligations (Il faut / On doit)
modules.kowae: Unit 4.2: What Needs To Be Done
modules.canDo: State what must or should be done using Il faut + infinitive or On doit + infinitive.
modules.concept: 'Il faut' ('it is necessary / we must') is followed directly by an infinitive verb ('partir', 'travailler', 'écouter')—no conjugation needed on the second verb!

model.en: We have to leave now. — Yes, we must begin tomorrow.
model.literal: [It is necessary = Il faut] + [to leave = partir] + [now = maintenant]

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.target: Tu es prêt ? Il faut partir maintenant.
turns.en: Are you ready? We have to leave now.

modules.title: Lesson 4.3: Explaining Why (parce que)
modules.canDo: Join two complete sentences to give a reason using parce que (because).
modules.concept: Connect any two statements with 'parce que' ('because'). Before a vowel sound (like 'il' or 'elle'), 'parce que' shortens to 'parce qu''.

model.context: Celebrating at the end of the day:
model.en: I am happy because the work is finished.
model.target: Je suis content parce que le travail est fini.
model.literal: [I am happy] + [because = parce que] + [the work is finished]

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.target: Je suis content parce que le travail est fini.
turns.en: I am happy because the work is finished.

check.question: Which phrase connects a statement to its reason ('because')?
